newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb blast at Kashmir communist rally kills four.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast at Kashmir communist rally kills four.

text.p: A bomb exploded during a communist rally on Wednesday in India's troubled Kashmir Valley, killing four people and injuring at least 15, police said.

The bomb went off in Kulgam town, 65 km (40 miles) south of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state. Yusuf Tarigami, state leader of the Communist Party of India-Marxist, was addressing supporters at the time, they said.
"Today during a public meeting held by M.Y. Tarigami in Kulgam area, militants fired a shot and followed it by hurling a grenade when the function was concluding," an official statement said.
Tarigami, who was voted to the state assembly in September, and one of his bodyguards were slightly injured, police said. Earlier they said the politician had escaped injury.
The September assembly elections were the first local polls in the Himalayan region since a violent separatist rebellion began in 1990.

Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died in the seven-year insurgency. India accuses Pakistan of arming and training guerrillas, but Islamabad says it offers them only moral and diplomatic support.
During the month-long electoral campaign, at least 21 people, most of them political activists, were killed in poll-related violence. Separatist groups boycotted the polls.
The state's new chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, whose pro-India National Conference party won a sweeping majority in the election, escaped two grenade attacks during the campaign.
A statement issued by Abdullah's office quoted him as condemning Wednesday's attack on the lone communist deputy in Kashmir's 87-member assembly.
"The chief minister asked the people to maintain vigilance against the nefarious designs of those rejected by them," the statement said.
"By resorting to attacks on soft targets, the militants were making a last ditch attempt to create terror in the situation," it said.
After he assumed power, Abdullah offered to sit down and talk with separatist leaders, but they rebuffed his proposal.
